Adds "Force paste" to the page right-click menu and as a browser command. It types the clipboard text into the focused field and bypasses sites that block pasting. Modifies browser_shortcut_metadata.cc, which is created by 107.
Shift+right-click always shows the browser's own context menu, even on sites that replace or block right-click. Setting in Appearance, on by default.

Crash-upload consent is forced off at Crashpad start, and channel-based auto-upload is disabled. Command-line switch values and feature parameters are stripped from crash reports, so they keep only names.

Adds a crash-reporting mode (Disabled / Ask / Automatic, default "Ask", shared by all profiles) and report deletion. Official builds upload to crash.helium.computer, overridable with the `--custom-crash-server-url` switch (not a flags entry). Policy can disable it. The crash dialog/UI is in another patch.
n: reports would go to Helium's server

w: Removes Google AI feature pages and resources from the build: Gemini in Chrome (glic), Lens overlay/side panel, Compose ("Help me write"), contextual tasks, the AI "actor" agent, AI overlay dialog, skills.
n: AI features that come back as opt-ins bring back what they need

w: Turns off the new web-based address-bar dropdown, including its AI-mode version, so the classic native dropdown is used. Also removes the experimental WebUI toolbar/browser pages and replaces a PNG icon with a vector icon.
DROPPED
DROPPED
The build uses the system `python3` instead of Chromium's bundled CPython. Build only.

When restoring a session at startup or reopening a closed window, background tabs (and pinned startup tabs) stay unloaded and show only their cached icon until you click them. Only the selected tab loads right away.
DROPPED

Splits the "google.com", "youtube.com" and "gstatic.com" strings so ungoogled-chromium's domain substitution leaves them intact. This keeps Google's browser-level exceptions working: login/session cookies on Google and YouTube, and security-key (U2F appid) enrollment on Google.
n: a website is a website: no special treatment for Google's sites

w: DROPPED
Replaces the shield icon used for Security/Privacy with a keyhole shield. In the settings sidebar, the Chrome logo next to "About" becomes a plain info icon.

Moves the "search suggestions" toggle from the privacy/Google-services area to the Search engine page. Also removes the "Sync and Google services" row and the sync setup pages from the profile settings.
n: the Firefox Sync row takes its place

w: Removes the whole "Autofill and passwords" section from the settings menu and pages: payments, addresses, ID documents, travel, shopping, Gemini suggestions and passkeys.
n: oganesson brings the Autofill and passwords section back

w: On the profile ("You and Google") page, removes the Google sign-in promo, the Google account row, "Google services", "Manage your Google Account", the "Profile name and picture" row and the "sync unavailable" notice.
Renames labels: the History page's menu item now says "History", and the "You and Google" settings page now uses the profile-menu name ("Profiles"/"Profile").
Removes the Safety Hub ("Safety check") page from Privacy settings and the Safety Hub suggestion on the Notifications page. It does this with an intentional `= false` assignment in route.ts.
When a search in settings finds nothing, the extra help line that links to Google help is no longer shown.

On the About page: removes the two "Learn more" links to support.google.com (about updating and about update errors), removes the click action on the product logo, hides the product subtitle line, and adjusts spacing.
Hides the whole Google Translate section of Languages settings (offer to translate, always/never translate lists) and the "translate target" label next to languages.
n: comes back with the translation opt-ins

w: Removes the Safety Hub header and buttons from the Site settings and Notifications pages, and the Safety Hub entry from the Privacy page. Goes with #16.
Shows the update status message and icon on the About page again (except on ChromeOS). An earlier patch had hidden them by setting the condition to `False`.

Hides the "Third-party cookies" row on the Privacy page. A search for cookies now points to Site settings instead. The Site settings description now reads "Manage site permissions and content settings (cookies, pop-ups, and more)".

Removes the Live Caption control from Accessibility settings on Windows and macOS, and removes the leftover divider lines above "Captions". Goes with the already dropped helium/core/disable-live-caption-completely.patch.
Rewords the help text above the third-party-cookie exceptions list into a plain explanation of the "[*.]" wildcard, without the tracking-protection wording.

Renames the search-suggest toggle to "Suggestions from the search engine". Its description now says Helium sends what you type in the address bar to your default search engine, and that this is off in Incognito.
Shows the "Reset to default theme" label on Linux too (stock hides it there). Shortens the auto-pin label to "Automatically pin new tab groups to the bookmarks bar", without "created on any device".

Settings now opens on "Appearance and behavior" instead of the profile/"You and Google" page. That item moves near the top of the sidebar, and the "AI" menu item is removed. Depends on #10 for the title and icon.

Adds an "Add" button to the main search engine list. It opens an "Add search engine" dialog with an "Add as default" button, which creates the engine and makes it the default in one step. Stock only lets you add site-search shortcuts.

In profile customization you can choose your own PNG or JPEG image (up to 30 MB) as the profile picture. It is cropped to a 256 px square, and you can clear it later; error messages cover files that are too large or unreadable. Depends on helium/core/custom-profile-avatar.patch.

Adds a "Keyboard shortcuts" page under System settings. You can search browser commands, add, remove or rebind shortcuts, see conflict warnings, and reset all to defaults. It only appears when the `CustomizableBrowserShortcuts` feature is on (on by default). Depends on helium/core/custom-keyboard-shortcuts.patch and the shortcut service.
In the "Delete browsing data" dialog, all data types are listed from the start (stock collapses them). The "Manage other Google data" link row is removed.

Adds a "Crash reporting" dropdown to Helium's services settings page: Disabled, Ask after a crash, or Send automatically. Choosing Disabled deletes pending reports, and the control locks if a policy disables metrics. Reports go to Helium's crash server (crash.helium.computer). The default is "Ask", set in helium/core/crash-reporting-prefs.patch, which this depends on.

Adds a "Fingerprinting protection" page under Privacy. It has an on/off toggle for Helium's noise feature, an explanation, and per-site exception and override lists. It only appears when the HeliumNoise feature is available. Depends on helium/core/noise/core.patch, where the protection is on by default.

Renames the "Security" page to "Network and security" and splits it into Network, Privacy signals and Security sections. Adds a "Global Privacy Control" toggle and moves "Do Not Track" there without its confirmation dialog. Removes the Do Not Track toggle, the "universal opt-out" toggle and section headers from the cookies page, and rewords the HTTPS warning labels. The GPC toggle depends on helium/core/network/global-privacy-control-pref.patch.
DROPPED

Makes the browser frame more compact. The address bar goes from 34 to 28 px tall, toolbar buttons from 34 to 28 px, and tabs from 35 to 31 px. Most toolbar and tab strip padding is based on a new 3 px "Helium base padding" constant, and address bar items get less rounded corners (radius 12 to 6).

Makes buttons, menus and dialogs across the native UI and the internal web pages less rounded. Buttons are rounded rectangles (7 px) instead of pills, menus and dialogs use 8 px corners, and web-page buttons have 8 px corners and never wrap their text.

Restyles the shared parts of chrome:// pages (Settings, History, Downloads, Extensions and others). It removes the Chrome logo from page headers and the side drawer, replaces round buttons and pill-shaped search boxes with rounded squares, flattens card shadows to thin outlines, and makes toasts and nav-menu items more compact. It also restyles the theme color picker and segmented buttons.

The new tab page is always the browser's own built-in page, whatever search engine is default. Stock Chromium gives that page only to Google users. With another engine it loads that engine's own new-tab URL or a bare "third-party" page. This also drops the supervised-user URL check and the Google-only special case.

Strips the new tab page down to the centered shortcut tiles and an icon-only Customize button. Removed: the Google bar at the top (an iframe loaded from Google), the Google logo, the search box and AI "composebox", voice search, Lens upload, the Microsoft auth iframe, cards/modules, action chips, promos, the wallpaper-search button, background-image credit and undo toasts.

Removes the curved corners where the toolbar meets the tab strip and around the page area, in both horizontal and vertical tab layouts, so edges are flat and square. It also removes the vertical tab strip's outline, shadow and "glass" transparency or blur effects when it expands on hover.

Reshapes the address bar into a rounded rectangle instead of a pill, with tighter icon and text spacing and a thin divider after the site-info label. It permanently hides several address-bar icons: AI Mode, Lens homework, Lens results, offers/rewards, cookie controls, payments/virtual card, autofill re-auth and filled-card info. chrome://, extension and file:// pages no longer show a text label next to the site icon.

Address-bar action icons (translate, bookmark star, etc.) are always plain icons with no expanded text label or tinted chip. The "Open in app" chip with the app's icon no longer appears; the plain app-picker icon shows instead.

Several tab strip changes:
- Every tab is drawn as a separate rounded box, and tabs are narrower (190 px instead of 232; split tabs are wider).
- The close "x" shows only when the mouse is over a tab.
- The speaker/alert icon sits next to the favicon, left of the title, and no longer fades in or out.
- Tab-group underlines and headers are restyled; buttons on the tab strip use tab colors.
- Clicking a tab's speaker icon to mute it is turned on by default (`kEnableTabMuting`: off to on).

Tabs no longer show the spinning loading ring around the favicon. Sleeping (discarded) tabs, and restored tabs that have not loaded yet, show a faded grayscale icon instead of Chrome's dotted ring, and Chrome's tip popup about discarded tabs is removed. The existing Performance setting is renamed "Differentiate hibernated tabs – Display hibernated tab icons in grayscale".

When you move between pages on the same site, the tab keeps showing the previous site icon until the new one loads, instead of flashing a blank globe. It also improves detection of pages that have no icon, including pages restored from the back/forward cache and pages whose security policy blocks the icon.
The new-tab "+" button and other tab strip buttons get 8 px rounded-square corners instead of being circles.

Toolbar buttons and their hover highlights are rounded squares instead of circles. The split-view toolbar button shows only if the user pinned it, not automatically when the current tab is in a split.
Removes the thin vertical dividers in the toolbar: the one before the extensions puzzle icon and the one in the pinned-actions area.

You can drag the window by any empty space in the toolbar, as with a title bar. Stock Chromium does this only in vertical-tabs mode. It also adds a macOS guard against a crash while a window is closing.

In Customize Chrome > Toolbar, users can hide the Back, Reload, profile avatar, Extensions, main Menu and Media controls buttons. It adds new prefs `helium.browser.show_back_button`, `show_reload_button`, `show_avatar_button`, `show_extensions_button`, `show_menu_button` and `show_media_button`, all default true, so nothing changes until the user turns one off. It also reorders and re-categorizes that settings list, and menus/popups still have an anchor in the top corner when the menu button is hidden.

Moves the Tab Search button (the list of open tabs) from the tab strip to the toolbar, with a new search-list icon instead of a down-arrow. It can be pinned in Customize Toolbar. If it is not pinned, it appears only while the tab search popup is open (opened by keyboard shortcut or menu) and disappears 2 seconds after the popup closes. Clicking it again closes the popup. The tab-strip combo button is removed from horizontal tabs, and the vertical tab strip's tab-search button is removed.

Makes the address-bar suggestion dropdown more compact. Rows shrink from 40px to 28px, the dropdown corners become 12px with a smaller shadow, and the highlighted row becomes a rounded box instead of a left-edge pill with a selection bar. Special icon backgrounds on action and journey suggestions are removed, indents are tightened, and the suggestion chips are restyled.

In the three-dot menu, the round in-menu buttons (the zoom +/- row) get 8px rounded-square highlights. The tinted row backgrounds behind the profile row, the "Update" row and the "Set as default browser" row are removed, so those rows look like normal items.

Reorganizes the three-dot menu. Removed: the profile submenu, "Passwords and autofill", "Send to your devices", Translate, "Reading mode", the vertical-tabs toggle, the Safety Hub notification row and the Reading List item under Bookmarks. "Bookmarks and lists" is renamed to "Bookmarks", and "Extensions" becomes one item that opens the extensions page instead of a submenu (no more Web Store promo). "Customize Chrome" moves from More tools to the main menu (not in Incognito or Guest). "Exit" moves into More tools. The "Update/relaunch" item moves from the very top into the normal notice area with a plain icon. Depends on helium/core/services-schema-nag.patch, which defines AddHeliumSchemaItem.
n: "Passwords and autofill" stays in the menu; Translate returns with the translation opt-in

w: The three-dot toolbar button always looks like a plain toolbar button. Chrome's colored, expanded pill with text (such as "Update" or "New Chrome available") is gone, along with its highlight colors. The button now also draws its border.
Removes the "Reading list" submenu from the Bookmarks submenu of the three-dot menu.

In split view, removes the small floating toolbar at the bottom-right corner of the inactive pane (it held the split menu button and favicon). The pane outline and screen-capture border now draw as plain rounded rectangles.

Right-clicking the divider between split-view panes now opens the split-view menu (swap, close one side, exit split, toggle orientation). The divider handle is thinner (2px instead of 4px). "Send feedback" (to Google) is removed from that menu. "Close left/right tab" is fixed for right-to-left languages in top/bottom layout. The split-view promo text color is softened.

Build/plumbing only. Adds helper functions that return Helium's window corner radii: 8px in general, 12px on macOS, 17px on macOS 26+, and a "padded" radius used by later patches. Uses kHeliumBasePadding from helium/ui/layout-constants.patch.

Restyles split view. The gap around panes shrinks (8px to 3px, inner padding 4px to 2px). Corner rounding uses Helium's radii, and the bottom outer corners of the panes match the window's own rounded corners (except in fullscreen or while a drop target is shown on that side). Uses frame-radius-helper.patch and builds on remove-split-view-mini-toolbar.patch.

Adds the setting "Show a rounded frame around web contents" under Settings > Appearance (pref helium.browser.rounded_frame, default ON). When on, even a single, unsplit page sits inside a small inset, rounded, outlined frame, like split view. The frame is turned off in fullscreen and in non-normal windows. Also fixes the reported page size so it excludes the border. Depends on multi-contents-view.patch and frame-radius-helper.patch. Its settings entry sits next to the Shift+right-click pref from helium/core/shift-right-click-context-menu.patch.

Removes the small curved corner piece where the toolbar separator meets an open side panel. The contents area now knows when a side panel is attached on the left or right, so it drops its inset and outer rounding on that side and draws a separator there instead. This makes the rounded frame meet the side panel cleanly. Builds on rounded-frame-corners.patch.

Restyles the "drop here to split" area that appears when you drag a link or tab to the page edge. It gets tighter padding, Helium corner radii and an outline, neutral instead of accent-colored icon and text, and a faster animation (450ms to 300ms). It also appears sooner: the delay drops from 1000ms to 500ms in three default feature parameters. It respects the rounded frame and an open side panel. Depends on frame-radius-helper.patch, rounded-frame-corners.patch and fix-layout-separators.patch.
The Customize side panel stops reacting to which kind of tab is active. It no longer jumps back to the overview page or changes its sections when you switch between the new tab page and other tabs.

Restyles the side panel. Margins shrink (8px to 3px on most sides, a wider 6px strip on the resize side), the header is shorter (40px to 32px) and the resize handle is thinner. Corner rounding follows Helium's radii, with the window-edge corner matching the window. The minimum width is lowered to 200px, and dragging snaps to the default width. Chrome's drop-shadow box around the side panel is disabled. Uses frame-radius-helper.patch.

Removes actions for features Helium doesn't use from the list of buttons you can pin to the toolbar or side panel. Removed: Reading list, Tabs from other devices, Shopping insights, Merchant trust, Google Lens / Lens overlay, price insights and discounts icons, Send tab to self, Translate, Addresses, Payment methods and Passwords. Translate, passwords and saved-card icons are also removed from installed web-app (PWA) title bars. Adds null checks so the code that used those actions doesn't crash. These are mostly Google-backed features or ones disabled by other patches (for example helium/core/disable-password-manager.patch).
n: the Password manager button stays available

w: Hides the "Autofill settings" and "Manage your Google Account" buttons in the profile menu.
The "extension installed" popup no longer shows the extra tips text: how to use it, its keyboard shortcut link and where to manage it. Only the title and icon remain.

If an extension download is blocked because Helium services or extension downloads are turned off, the downloads bubble says "Extension downloads are disabled" instead of "Blocked by your organization". It also offers a button that opens chrome://settings/privacy/services. Relies on helium::GetDummyURL from the Helium-services patches (for example helium/core/services-prefs.patch and helium/core/proxy-extension-downloads.patch).
n: works only with Helium's services, which are off; you can turn them on in Settings

w: When you switch the address bar to a search engine with Tab (keyword mode), the chip shows just the engine's name (for example "DuckDuckGo") instead of "Search DuckDuckGo". The chip's padding and spacing are also tightened.
Bookmark-bar buttons and folders get a 6px rounded-rectangle hover highlight instead of a fully round pill shape.

New tab page shortcut tiles are restyled. Icons sit in rounded squares instead of circles, tiles have 10px corners instead of 4px, and favicons are larger (30px, fetched at 128px so they stay sharp). Spacing is slightly adjusted.

Tightens the look of all web-based side panels (bookmarks, history, customize, and so on). Corners are smaller (12px to 9px), padding and gaps between cards are smaller, headings are shorter, and the hidden back button no longer takes up space. Search fields are rounded.

Simplifies the Customize side panel. The theme preview picture, the uploaded/searched-image and "managed by" rows, the mini toolbar illustration, the category titles, the intro text and the reorder tip card are all removed. Theme editing becomes a "Change wallpaper" button that goes straight to uploading your own image instead of opening the theme gallery. "Reset to classic Chrome" becomes a "Reset to default" button. The "Shortcuts" heading is removed and spacing is tightened. Builds on side-panel-webui-general.patch.
Swaps the Chrome logo icon used in the browser's internal pages (for example the "About" entry in Settings) for Helium's star-shaped logo.
The letter tiles shown for sites that have no icon (on new-tab shortcuts and similar places) are drawn as rounded squares with a fixed 14px corner radius, not circles.

New profiles start with the grey (grayscale) theme. "Reset to default" also returns to grey, and the stock blue "Default" swatch is removed from the theme colour picker. Pref kGrayscaleThemeEnabled is set to true for new profiles; in stock Chromium it is false.

Redesigns the small pop-up notifications (toasts, such as "Link copied"). They are smaller (32px instead of 48px), have 8px corners, a thin outline and no shadow, use the address-bar colour, appear at the right side under the toolbar instead of centred, and scale in instead of sliding down. Also changes when a toast is drawn over the page, so it no longer depends on fullscreen state.
Buttons on security warning pages (for example "Your connection is not private") get 8px corners instead of pill shapes, and slightly narrower padding.
When there is no saved window position, the first browser window opens centred on the screen, not near the top-left corner.

Removes several items from Developer Tools: the Recorder's "Send feedback" link, the "What's New" panel, the Gemini rebrand promo pop-up, the Help submenu in the DevTools menu, and the Google account sync / Google Developer Program badges section in DevTools settings.

Removes Chrome's own first-run intro page and "feature showcase" page, the first-run intro sounds, the Password Manager "share with family" banner images, the Gemini settings image and the Google Drive sign-in promo picture. Most users will not notice, because Helium shows its own onboarding instead. Depends on the helium_onboarding component, which another Helium patch adds.
Makes the bookmarks bar tighter: separators are thinner (1px instead of 2px) and have less space around them, and the end margins are smaller.
On the "Who's using Helium?" profile picker, removes the decorative side banner images and the hidden action when you click the logo, and spaces the footer controls evenly.
The tab-group edit bubble no longer shows the "learn more about saved groups" footer, which stock Chromium shows up to 5 times.
Removes the illustration at the top of the new-profile customization dialog and makes the header shorter (130px instead of 170px).
DROPPED

Infobars (the yellow-style bars under the toolbar, such as "Restore pages?") are shorter (44px instead of 56px) and use the toolbar colour. The drop shadow under them is replaced by thin side separators that fit Helium's rounded or attached content frame. Depends on rounded-frame-corners.patch (pref helium.browser.rounded_frame, default true, and ShouldUseRoundedFrame) and on Helium's vertical tab layout code.
Text buttons across the browser UI are 2px shorter (1px less padding above and below).

Installed web apps get a tighter title-bar toolbar with smaller margins, and the page title is no longer shown next to the address in the app's top bar. Uses kHeliumBasePadding, which layout-constants.patch defines.

Overhauls the built-in colours. In light mode the window frame matches the toolbar, and an inactive window keeps the same frame colour. The address bar is slightly see-through (80% opaque). Background tabs are transparent with a faint highlight on hover. The selected tab uses the address-bar colour, and separators and bubble borders are toned down in dark mode. On Linux, the system-theme tab colours change to match. Custom themes are not affected.

The tab strip area paints the window frame or theme background itself, and in fullscreen the area behind the tabs uses the theme image instead of a plain colour. Visually this keeps themes consistent behind the tabs. Depends on ThemedBackground::kFrameTheme / CustomCornersBackground::FrameTheme(), which remove-toolbar-corners.patch adds.

The link-preview bubble in the bottom-left corner (shows the URL when you hover a link) becomes a floating rounded pill with 16px corners, a soft shadow and a thin outline. It is inset 8px from the window corner and uses address-bar colours, instead of the square box attached to the corner.

The Incognito and Guest new tab pages lose their "Learn more" links (to Google help pages) and the Incognito page loses the third-party cookie blocking box. The Incognito description is rewritten for Helium and no longer mentions Google.

Turns on Chromium's overlay scrollbar feature (kOverlayScrollbar, mode "device") by default on Windows and Linux too, not only on Mac/ChromeOS. Web page scrollbars then follow the OS setting, so they can be thin overlay scrollbars that hide when not in use.

Replaces Chromium's Google-blue colour palette with Helium's indigo/blue (#3450d1) and slightly different greys, in the native UI, the internal pages (Settings, chrome://flags and so on) and the theme picker's grey swatch. Accent colours, highlights and buttons look different everywhere.

Restyles chrome://flags with rounded search box and dropdowns, an outline focus ring and full flag descriptions on narrow windows. The "Default" choice now shows its actual state, such as "Default (Enabled)", with a * and a footnote when a command line or variations has changed it.

The bundled uBlock Origin, a hidden built-in component, now appears on chrome://extensions with a blue "Helium component" badge using the Helium logo, so you can see and manage it. Other extensions can see it via chrome.management but cannot uninstall it through that API. Depends on Manifest::IsUBlockComponent from the core uBlock patches (for example ublock-helium-services.patch) and on the logo from helium-logo-icons.patch.

Adds licence entries for Helium itself (GPL-3.0), the Instrument Sans font and Tabler Icons, so they appear on the chrome://credits page. Build and licensing only. Refers to files in components/helium_onboarding, which another patch adds.
The password autofill drop-down on login forms no longer shows its footer, such as "Manage passwords" and passkey/other-device entries.
n: the password manager is kept, so its link stays

w: macOS only: moves the red/yellow/green window buttons closer to the window corner (10px inset) and adjusts the space reserved for them and the window corner radius on macOS 26.

The Find-in-page (Ctrl+F) box now sits at the top-right corner of the web page, not hanging under the address bar. It has tighter padding and a smaller shadow, and the magnifier icon no longer appears in the address bar while it is open.

Connects Helium's customizable keyboard shortcuts to browser windows. User-defined shortcuts replace the built-in ones and apply live when changed, and on Mac they also update the menu-bar shortcuts. Depends on core/custom-keyboard-shortcuts.patch, which defines BrowserShortcutService and flag kCustomizableBrowserShortcuts (enabled by default); settings/custom-keyboard-shortcuts-page.patch provides the editor UI.

After the browser restarts from a crash, a dialog asks "Would you like to send a crash report?" with "Send report", "No thanks" and "Don't ask again" (sets reporting to disabled). Reports that are not sent are deleted. Sent reports go to Helium's server (https://crash.helium.computer/crash, set in core/crash-reporting-prefs.patch). Depends on crash-reporting-prefs.patch: pref kHeliumCrashReportingMode, default kAsk.

The chrome://crashes page follows Helium's crash-reporting setting (automatic, ask or disabled) instead of Google metrics consent. It always lists local crashes, shows the Helium version, and its "Create an issue with details" link opens a GitHub issue on imputnet/helium, not the Chromium bug tracker. Depends on core/crash-reporting-prefs.patch and on core/add-helium-versioning.patch (GetHeliumVersionNumber).
n: its issue link points at oganesson

w: Groundwork for Helium's layout system. It replaces Chromium's on/off "vertical tabs" setting with one setting, `helium.browser.layout`, that holds one of four layouts: Classic (the default), Compact, Vertical or Dynamic. It also adds a setting for vertical tabs on the right side (default off). Visible side effects: the vertical-tabs "expand on hover" option is forced off and its tip popup is removed, the "try vertical tabs" promo popup is removed, and the collapsed state and width of the vertical tab strip are no longer saved per window in session restore.

On the Appearance settings page, the stock "Tab strip position (side/top)" dropdown is replaced by a "Browser layout" dropdown (Classic/Dynamic/Compact/Vertical; Classic is the default). A "Show vertical tabs on right side" toggle appears when Vertical is chosen. Several stock toggles are removed from that page: expand vertical tabs on hover, organizer panel button, "everything menu" button, auto-show tab scroll buttons, and "Show tab search button".

Right-clicking the window title bar now shows a "Browser layout" submenu with check items for Classic/Dynamic/Compact/Vertical, plus "Tabs on right side" when Vertical is active. The submenu is not shown in incognito windows. The stock title-bar menu items for vertical tabs are removed: show tabs vertically/horizontally, collapse/expand, expand on hover, send feedback, and pin tab scroll buttons.

In the Vertical layout, Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on Mac) collapses or expands the vertical tab strip instead of saving the page. This is on by default, and a toggle on the settings behavior page turns it off; in other layouts Ctrl+S still saves the page. It also removes Chromium's Ctrl+Shift+L shortcut for collapsing vertical tabs, and on Mac it removes the Cmd+Alt+N shortcut for a new split tab.
n: Ctrl+S always saves the page here: the switch is off by default. Collapsing the vertical tabs gets Firefox's Ctrl+Alt+Z, if free

w: Adds an optional "Centered address bar" setting (off by default). When on, the address bar is narrowed by 5–12% of the toolbar width (at most 700 px wide) and centered in the window. The toggle is hidden in the Compact layout.
Changes the empty space reserved at the end of the tab strip for dragging the window: stock Chromium uses 42 px, this uses 27 px in the Classic layout and none in the other layouts.
Hides the "+" new tab button (and the divider after the last tab) in the horizontal tab strip when the layout is Dynamic or Vertical. Classic and Compact keep it.

In every layout except Classic, the toolbar becomes the top row of the window, next to the window buttons. In Compact, the address bar gets a fixed 350 px width. The Back and Reload buttons no longer shrink or move into the overflow menu. The stock rule that lets the address bar keep its size longest when space is tight is removed.
Adds an optional "Minimal URL in the address bar" setting (off by default). When on and the address bar is not focused, it shows only the site's domain, centered; clicking into it shows the full URL.

Implements the Dynamic layout: the toolbar is on top and the horizontal tab strip sits below it, and the tab strip is hidden while the window has only one tab. Also adjusts frame painting for this layout on Linux.

Implements the Compact layout: the tabs move into the toolbar row to the right of the address bar, giving one combined bar. The "+" button is hidden when it does not fit, and centering of the address bar is turned off in this layout.

Restyles Chromium's vertical tabs for the Vertical layout. The tab strip can sit on the right side. The button row at the top of the strip and the floating rounded corners are removed. The bottom button becomes a labeled "New tab" button. The strip is narrower: default width 200 instead of 240, collapsed 42 instead of 56, minimum 160 instead of 126. Resizing snaps to the default width, the collapse animation is shorter (250 ms), and the divider between pinned and unpinned tabs is removed. In each tab, the sound icon sits next to the site icon, and clicking it to mute is disabled while the strip is collapsed. Spacing and tab-group lines are tightened. It also removes "Show tabs vertically/horizontally" from the tab right-click menu and "Pin tab search" from the title-bar menu.

Improves the toolbar on narrow windows. The extensions (puzzle) button can now move into the "..." overflow menu, and the overflow menu no longer has separators. The split-tabs button moves into the overflow menu sooner. In Compact, the toolbar buttons keep their size and the tabs shrink first. When the puzzle button is hidden, extension popups open from the overflow button.

Adds two toolbar buttons, both on by default and both hideable from the Customize Toolbar panel. In the Vertical layout, a sidebar-icon button collapses or expands the vertical tabs; it sits at the far left of the toolbar, or at the far right when tabs are on the right. In the Dynamic layout, a "+" new tab button appears in the toolbar, replacing the tab-strip "+" that horizontal-tabs.patch hides. Both buttons can move into the overflow menu.

Adds the settings and plumbing for "Frameless mode" (zen mode): an Appearance toggle "Automatically hide browser UI until you hover the window edge" (off by default), with sub-toggles "Always show the sidebar" (Vertical only) and "Always show the top bar" (both off by default). It also adds the Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+L shortcut to pin the top bar (disabled here) and a "New tab opened" toast. It renames the accessibility toast setting to "Background action confirmation toasts" with a new description. The actual hiding behavior is not in this patch.
Lets Frameless mode fade out and disable the window's close/minimize/maximize buttons on Mac, Linux and Windows while the browser UI is hidden.

Adds "Zen mode": the toolbar, tab strip and vertical tab sidebar hide and slide back in when the mouse reaches the top or side edge of the window. They stay visible while the address bar is focused or a menu or popup is open, and hide again when the window loses focus. The top bar and the sidebar can each be "pinned" to stay visible. In Zen mode Ctrl+S shows or hides the side tabs, and a toast says "new tab created" when a link opens a tab you can't see. Also fixes how many pinned tabs fit per row in the vertical tab strip, and clips the address bar and toolbar icons on Linux.

The browser window can be made narrower: 400px instead of 500px. The minimum width is now the same in every layout and no longer grows when vertical tabs or a side panel are open, so those panels may overlap at very small widths.

The "Create QR code" dialog makes plain square QR codes with no Chrome dinosaur in the middle, instead of Chrome's round dots, rounded corners and dino logo. Without the logo the code can also be smaller.

Makes the built-in PDF viewer more compact: the toolbar is 36px tall instead of 56px, with smaller text and padding. The sidebar is narrower (it widens only for the bookmarks or attachments tabs), and the selected page thumbnail gets a thin outline instead of a thick glow. It also removes the "Save to Google Drive" button from the PDF toolbar, and makes a small structural change to the History page's "Tabs from other devices" tab.
Hides the Live Caption button in the picture-in-picture video window, and its captions panel can never open.

Turns off the circular "ripple" animation when clicking buttons, both in the browser's own toolbar and menus and in its internal pages (Settings and other chrome:// pages). Clicks give no ripple feedback, like Chrome on Mac.
Fixes thin visible lines or gaps between parts of the browser window on screens with fractional scaling (such as 125% or 150%). Smoothing is now used only on rounded shapes, not on plain rectangles.
Windows only: changes how the top of the window is measured above the tab strip, so the tabs and toolbar sit in the right place.

macOS only: adds an option to make the browser frame (tab strip, toolbar, sidebar, infobars) see-through with the system's frosted-glass blur, tinted with the theme color. The option is a flag "Native frame materials" in chrome://flags, off by default. When the flag is on, a "Use native frame materials (experimental)" toggle appears in Settings > Appearance, also off by default (pref `helium.browser.native_frame_materials` = false).

When a page is zoomed in or out, the address bar shows the zoom level as small text (for example "125%") instead of Chrome's magnifier icon. Clicking it resets the zoom to 100%, where Chrome would open a zoom popup, and the zoom popup no longer appears on its own when zooming. Adds a "Show the zoom indicator in the address bar" toggle in Settings > Appearance, on by default (pref `helium.browser.show_zoom_indicator` = true).
Adds 133% and 140% to the zoom steps you go through with Ctrl+plus and Ctrl+minus, between 125% and 150%.
DROPPED

On the History page, "Tabs from other devices" now lists synced tabs when tab sync is on even if you are not signed in to a Google account. This supports sync services that are not tied to a Google account. Sign-in and sync prompts are hidden once tab sync is on.
t: Synced tabs without a Google account

w: When an extension starts debugging the browser, a small bug icon with "Debugging started" appears at the left of the address bar, instead of Chrome's full-width yellow bar across the page. Clicking the icon opens a popup listing the extensions and a "Stop" button for each. The old yellow bar is still used when there is no address bar visible.

Shows page-loading progress as a thin animated, glowing line along the bottom edge of the address bar, in the theme's accent color. Adds a "Show loading progress in the address bar" toggle in Settings > Appearance, on by default (pref `helium.browser.show_progress_bar` = true).

Restyles the "Press Esc to exit full screen" message: rounded corners, no shadow, dark grey background, smaller text and tighter key labels. It stays for 2.5 seconds instead of 3.8, and fades in and out faster. The background is always solid, whatever Chrome's transparency setting says.

Adds a flag "Hide all page actions" in chrome://flags, off by default. When it is on, every icon at the right end of the address bar is hidden, such as the bookmark star, zoom, install app and file access.
Expired chrome://flags entries stay listed and usable, marked with a warning that they may stop working or disappear soon.
Adds the shared plumbing that lets oganesson's own settings, strings and preferences plug into the browser without patching each feature in separately.
Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab show up under Next tab and Previous tab in the shortcut editor, with separate recently-used cycling commands when that mode is on.
New Scroll to top and Scroll to bottom commands that you can bind to a keyboard shortcut or mouse gesture.
Mouse gestures can run extensions' own commands, just as if their keyboard shortcut had been pressed.
The Shortcuts and gestures settings page lets you add, see, search and remove mouse gestures for every browser and extension command.
Hides the empty Passkeys entry in saved-info settings, since Linux has no passkey store without Google Password Manager.
Right-button stroke, rocker and wheel mouse gestures work anywhere in the window, including internal pages, PDFs, tabs, toolbar and side panel.
Middle-clicking empty space on the horizontal tab strip opens a new tab, as in Firefox.
Middle-clicking empty space in the vertical tab strip opens a new tab, and clicks at the window edge reach the tabs.
Sign in with a Mozilla account, or point it at your own sync server, which works best. Passwords, bookmarks, history, open tabs, addresses and cards sync between oganesson, tennessine and Firefox.
The You and Sync settings page offers Firefox Sync sign-in and controls, and hides Google account and Google-only autofill sections.
No Helium servers by default: Helium services, bangs, update checks, crash reports, onboarding and fingerprint noise are off but can be turned on.
The built-in uBlock Origin refreshes its filter list catalog from GitHub directly, so lists stay current with Helium's services off.
Firefox-style internal addresses such as about:addons, about:preferences, about:logins and about:support open the matching browser pages.
Release builds can target a newer x86-64 CPU level, such as x86-64-v2, for faster code on modern processors.
The built-in password manager offers to save passwords by default, and you can turn that off in settings.
Every toolbar item, including the address bar, buttons and pinned extensions, can be dragged anywhere and hidden, and the layout survives restarts.
Tab search sits on the toolbar instead of the tab strip, Chrome Labs is removed, and the Home button is shown or hidden from Customize toolbar.
Cycling tabs in recently-used order with Ctrl+Tab keeps working correctly when tabs are closed or moved during the cycle.
When recording a new keyboard shortcut, keys like Ctrl+T are captured instead of running, and Enter reliably saves the shortcut.
Installing and updating extensions from the Chrome Web Store reports the browser version, so the store serves compatible extension builds.
Installed web apps open outside links in your default browser, and each app gets editable scope rules, exclusions and a custom start address.
New tabs open and closing a tab selects the next one by Firefox's rules, for links, extensions and pinned tabs alike.
Reloading or updating an extension like uBlock Origin no longer leaves a page that was loading stuck blank.
An about:config page lists every browser preference and lets you edit it, like Firefox's about:config.
Exposes menu item labels to UI DevTools so the automated browser tests can check menu contents.
Switches to stop saving browsing history, download history and closed tabs (optionally kept in memory for the session); Firefox Sync then skips history too.
Privacy and security settings show the Don't save browsing history, Don't save download history and keep-closed-tabs switches.
Open tabs from your other Firefox Sync devices appear in History's Tabs from other devices and the app menu's Recent tabs.
Your Mozilla account's name and picture show on the profile button across restarts, which says Sync paused when you must sign in again.
Removes the media controls button that pops into the toolbar while media plays; Cast stays in the app menu.
Firefox-like address bar: choose and reorder suggestion sources, match bookmarks anywhere in title or address, and autofill sites from bookmarks and history.
An Address bar suggestions section in search engine settings with switches for history, bookmarks, open tabs and past searches, plus a suggestion order.
Firefox-style autoplay control: allow everything, block audio, or block audio and video until you click or type in the page itself.
Site settings get an Autoplay page with the three choices and per-site Allow or Block exceptions.
Tabs hide the sound-playing icon unless you turn it on, while muted, camera, microphone and screen-sharing icons always show.
Appearance settings get a Show sound icon on tabs switch.
On Wayland, dropping a link onto the split-view panel works even if the pointer stops moving before you release it.
Brands the browser as oganesson everywhere, with internal pages shown as oganesson:// while chrome:// still works.
On Linux the browser runs as oganesson with its own desktop entry and its own profile in ~/.config/oganesson, moving an old oganesson-focused profile there.
On Windows the browser installs and keeps its profile under %LOCALAPPDATA%\oganesson with its own file associations, URL scheme and policy key.
The Windows installer and zip ship the Firefox Sync library and the NSS files it needs, so Sync works on Windows.
Lets the Windows installer be packed on a Linux build machine using its own 7-Zip.
Built on Helium, carrying its whole patch series, including full uBlock Origin with Manifest V2 support built in.
Keeps useful features such as the password manager, Sync and Google search, but each is optional: DuckDuckGo is the default and Sync stays off until you sign in.
New profiles get one search engine list everywhere with DuckDuckGo first, the EU choice screen, and no search engine favicon fetching.
Signed apt and dnf repositories for Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora deliver updates with your normal system updates.
Runs on Linux x86-64 on X11 and Wayland; release builds target x86-64-v2 machines.
A Windows x64 build, cross-compiled on Linux, ships as an installer for one or all users and a portable zip, without an auto-updater.
Keeps its own profile, separate from Helium's and Chromium's.

Update policy: a new release in the current Chromium milestone at once (experimentally, the two browsers may differ within a milestone), a new milestone once Helium and Vanadium both have it, and fixes for exploits in the wild at once.
oganesson's own strings come with Polish translations.
Automated browser tests cover gestures, toolbar, tab behavior, web app links, autoplay, address bar suggestions and Sync before release.
Settings > Toolbar layout lets you reorder the toolbar's items, address bar included, and hide any except the address bar and menu.
Hide toolbar on scroll is a switch, off by default; when on, the toolbar hides as soon as a page loads, without Chromium's 3-second delay.
With the address bar at the bottom, the menu, search suggestions and tab switcher all run upward from it, the most-used item nearest your thumb.
The new tab page keeps the address bar where you put it, instead of moving it to the top, and drops its own search box.
Fixes a Chromium bug where, after swiping the toolbar between tabs, the toolbar stayed stuck on screen while the page scrolled under it.
The tab switcher is a compact vertical list (favicon, title, close button) instead of thumbnail cards; swipe-to-close, reordering and groups still work.
The address bar always shows the full URL, including https:// and www.
Page zoom follows Android's font size: a smaller system font makes whole pages smaller, multiplied with the default zoom setting.
The JavaScript JIT runs by default for speed; Vanadium's per-site setting stays, so you can still block it for any site.
On first run the browser downloads Helium's uBlock Origin build, checks it against a pinned SHA-256 and installs it as an extension, with Helium's extension ID, so its settings carry over.
The extensions puzzle button stays on the toolbar while no extension is pinned, so your extensions never end up out of reach.
A Firefox Sync account row sits at the top of Settings, like Firefox for Android, opening the Sync settings screen.
Ships Firefox Sync's Rust library, built for arm64, and its translated strings in the APK.
Privacy settings get switches to stop saving browsing history, closed tabs and download history, next to Close tabs on exit.
In installed web apps, a link's long-press menu opens it in your default browser, launched behind the web app; with tennessine as default, it becomes a background tab.
Settings > Autofill services names the built-in option "Autofill with Tennessine", using passwords, addresses and cards saved in the browser, Firefox Sync's included, not Google.
Settings > Last crash shows the stack trace of the last Java crash, so you can share it without adb.
Native libraries are stored compressed and the unused XR (headset/ARCore) module is dropped, so each download is about 190 MB instead of 340 MB.
Vanadium's hardening: compiler flags, memory tagging, W^X, and strict site and origin isolation.
Vanadium's state partitioning and attack-surface cuts, such as sensors, WebGPU and payments.
DuckDuckGo is the default search engine, with seven engines to choose from, Google among them.
A local password store that works without a Google account; Firefox Sync passwords build on it.
t: Password store without a Google account

w: Bookmark import and export, a barcode detector without Play services, and a WebRTC settings screen.
Off-by-default toggles to open external links and custom tabs in incognito, and a toggle to close tabs on exit.
Chrome extensions on a phone: a toolbar button, extension popups, and pinning extensions to the toolbar.
Manifest V2 extensions keep working.
Install extensions from the Chrome Web Store, Opera and Edge add-on sites, or unpacked from phone storage.
Extensions can run in incognito tabs.
DevTools on the phone.
Titanium's feature overrides, accessibility fixes, un-expired flags and fixes for Chromium bugs.
Site search from the address bar, with the address bar kept in phone behavior.
Install from the project's F-Droid repository (https://packages.zakius.xyz/fdroid/repo) in F-Droid or Obtainium, with background updates.
The APK's native libraries are deflated with Zopfli before signing, since F-Droid and Obtainium have no delta updates and download size is each update's cost.
Dropped from Vanadium: HTTPS-Only mode, the built-in ad filter (uBlock Origin replaces it) and GrapheneOS connectivity checks that ping GrapheneOS servers.
One settings page with a separate, off-by-default switch for each Google-backed feature, each saying what it sends and to whom.
lets autofill ask Google which form fields are which (crowdsourcing).
page translation through Google, with the Translate settings and menu item back.
Chromium's local translation; downloads only its language packs.
Google Cloud Messaging for web push while no tab of the site is open.
one switch for mDNS and DIAL discovery and all of casting.
Gemini in the browser, AI skills, AI permission prompts, page annotation models, Screen AI.
Tab-strip scrolling (off everywhere), close the window with the last tab, clear data on exit, close confirmation and a custom new tab page move from chrome://flags into Settings.
Passwords and autofill back in the app menu, the Password manager toolbar action, the "Manage passwords" footer on login forms, and password import if it works.
Settings > Behavior > Tab behavior: a Firefox (default) or Chromium preset over five rules for where new tabs open and which tab is selected after closing one, or any custom mix.
